What the simulations are saying

  • The favorite is still an underdog to the field. The San Antonio Spurs win the NBA title in 20% of 10,000 simulated postseasons, the best of any club, which means someone else wins it in 80% of them. Four rounds of best of seven is a long way to go, even for the best team.
  • The conference favorites. In the Eastern the Detroit Pistons reach the NBA Finals 25% of the time; In the Western the San Antonio Spurs reach the NBA Finals 30% of the time.
  • The play-in is a real risk for good teams. The club most likely to end up there is the Golden State Warriors, in the play-in 55% of the time. Finishing seventh or eighth means one extra game, finishing ninth or tenth means two wins in a row on the road just to reach the first round.
  • Too close to call. The Orlando Magic (63%), the Phoenix Suns (55%), the Toronto Raptors (52%), the Golden State Warriors (47%), the Memphis Grizzlies (39%) make the playoffs in between 35% and 65% of simulated seasons. Those are the clubs whose next few weeks move the bracket most.

How the 2026-27 NBA playoffs work

Each conference sends six teams straight to the playoffs. The teams that finish seventh through tenth play the play-in tournament: seven hosts eight and the winner takes the 7 seed, nine hosts ten and the loser goes home, and the loser of seven against eight hosts the winner of nine against ten for the 8 seed. That is why the bracket above has a play-in column: a 9 or 10 seed has to win twice on the road to reach the first round.

The first round is 1 against 8, 4 against 5, 2 against 7 and 3 against 6. The bracket is fixed, there is no reseeding, so the 1 seed's second round opponent is always the winner of 4 against 5. Every series is best of seven, played 2-2-1-1-1: the team with the better regular season record hosts games one, two, five and seven. Home court in the NBA Finals goes to the team with the better record, whichever conference it comes from.

How the bracket odds are produced

The percentage beside each team in the bracket is that team's chance to win that matchup. Play-in games are single games; every other round is a best of seven, and the chance is worked out exactly, game by game, from the model's single game win probability at each arena in the 2-2-1-1-1 order, so home court counts for what it is worth and no more. Your champion card multiplies every pick you made into the model's odds of that exact bracket, which is why a bracket full of favorites is still a long shot.

The seeds start from the projected standings: every team's average wins across 10,000 simulated 2026-27 seasons, from the same game model the NBA Season Simulator uses. Edit seeds lets you set any field you like. The odds table is a different question answered the same way: it plays the regular season and the whole postseason 10,000 times and counts how often each club reaches each round. How the model has scored on a season it never saw is on the season simulator and on the methodology page.

Simulations are useful. Verified records matter more.

A simulator can tell you what might happen. It cannot tell you who has actually been right. NBA Playoff Simulator FAQ

What is an NBA playoff simulator?

A tool that plays out the NBA postseason. Here it does two jobs: a bracket picker where you choose the winner of every play-in game and series through the NBA Finals, and a predictor that simulates the 2026-27 season and playoffs 10,000 times to give every team's odds of reaching each round.

How do I fill out an NBA playoff bracket?

Click a team in any matchup to advance it. Later rounds fill in as you go, and changing an early pick clears only the picks that depended on it. Fill with favorites takes the model's favorite in every open matchup, Simulate the rest draws them from the model's odds, and Edit seeds lets you change the field before you start.

How does the NBA play-in tournament work?

Seven hosts eight and the winner is the 7 seed. Nine hosts ten and the loser is out. The loser of seven against eight then hosts the winner of nine against ten, and that winner is the 8 seed. The bracket above plays all three games.

Who is favored to win the 2026-27 NBA title?

In the current projection the San Antonio Spurs win it 20% of the time, ahead of the Oklahoma City Thunder at 16%. Those numbers move as results come in, and the page is rebuilt twice a day.

Can I share my NBA bracket?

Yes. Share bracket copies a link that carries your seeds and picks, and anyone who opens it sees the same bracket. Your bracket is also kept on your own device, so it is still there when you come back.

Is the NBA playoff simulator free?

Yes. The bracket picker, the projected field and the published odds are always free. Your first simulation on TrustMyRecord is free, with no account needed. After that, a free account gives you one free run a day on every simulator. For more runs, TMR Pro members run every simulator without limits. A run only counts once its result appears, so a run that fails or never finishes costs nothing.
